champion: Pleomorphic adenoma of minor salivary gland
ordered_diagnoses: Pleomorphic adenoma of minor salivary gland

s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic facial swelling with reduced mouth opening and prior similar episodes
salient_findings: Asymptomatic swelling in the right lower half of the face
Ovoid subcutaneous swelling with ill-defined borders
Elevated and glistening right buccal mucosa
key_facts: 62-year-old man
Two-week history of facial swelling
Two prior similar episodes over eight years
No pain or fever
Known diabetic on regular medication
6 × 6 cm ovoid subcutaneous swelling
Swelling extended from the level of the right lateral canthus to 1 cm below the corner of the mouth
Restricted mouth opening due to the mass
Contrast-enhanced CT showed a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas
Intracystic loculations with dense cystic content
Erosion of the posterior buccal cortex without perforation of the maxilla
Maxillary antrum was compressed

shortlist.label: Buccal space abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical diagnosis and imaging findings of a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas in the right buccal space

shortlist.label: Dentigerous cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of a cystic lesion in the jaw, although less likely given the clinical presentation and imaging findings

shortlist.label: Sialadenitis
shortlist.why_kept: Inflammation of the salivary gland could cause facial swelling, but the location and characteristics of the mass make this less likely

shortlist.label: Odontogenic myxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that could present as a jaw lesion, but the clinical and imaging findings are not typical for this diagnosis

raw.champion: Pleomorphic adenoma of minor salivary gland
raw.rationale: The lesion's characteristics, such as its long history, lack of pain or fever, well-defined borders on CT, and leathery pouch-like appearance, are more consistent with a benign salivary gland tumor like pleomorphic adenoma than an abscess or other options.

rejected.label: Buccal space abscess
rejected.why: The absence of pain, fever, and lymphadenopathy, along with the lesion's long history and well-defined borders, make an abscess less likely.

rejected.label: Dentigerous cyst
rejected.why: The location and description of the lesion do not suggest an association with an unerupted tooth, which is typical for dentigerous cysts.

rejected.label: Sialadenitis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings do not indicate inflammation of the salivary gland, which is characteristic of sialadenitis.

rejected.label: Odontogenic myxoma
rejected.why: While possible, the description provided does not specifically suggest the gelatinous appearance typical of odontogenic myxomas, and the location is not as commonly associated with this tumor type as with salivary gland tumors.
